review.rationale: Option A correctly identifies that a fixed pre-Decision tracked JSON count is inherently unstable because the governance chain itself must commit auditable JSON artifacts before execution. Binding the complete runtime manifest via git ls-files --full-name at the remote-verified execution HEAD provides a deterministic, reproducible completeness proof that adapts to legitimate governance additions while preserving validation scope over all tracked JSON. The three-stage validation order (parse/duplicate, schema, cross-file consistency) is sound, the frozen five-path patch binding is preserved, and the fail-closed boundary correctly rejects any count mismatch, parse failure, or scope reduction. Non-authorizations are complete and authority boundaries are preserved.
